intro: A G♭-major melody rides above triplet-motion broken chords, with a more accented minor middle section and a written-out return. The score is aligned automatically; timings remain provisional and unchecked by ear, particularly through the transition and quiet close.
question: What changes beneath the melody when it returns?

sections.label: A′ · written-out return, bars 55–74
sections.mNote: written-out return shortens and chromatically alters the familiar phrase

relations.label: The G♭ melody returns
relations.basis: The outer melody returns after the contrasting E♭-minor-centred middle. The 218.5 s measured offset agrees with the A′ marker near 218 s; the later continuation and coda are not assumed identical. CENS diagonal mean 0.964, sustained 39.5 s, fixed pitch-class shift 0 semitones and time offset 218.5 s (cache/form/schubert-impromptu-gflat.txt, candidate 1; 0.5 s grid). These are matched excerpts, not complete section boundaries; timing has not been checked by ear.

cues.title: A melody above triplets
cues.text: The melody begins on B♭, the third of G♭ major, while broken chords move in triplet subdivisions beneath it. Listen for the difference between the long upper notes, the faster inner movement and the slower bass: one pianist sustains all three layers.
cues.evidence: Bars 1–4, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. HautI begins with long B♭s; hautII writes B♭–D♭–G♭ figures in 6:4 and 3:2 groups; basIa begins G♭–D♭, then E♭ and C♭ basses. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Listen beneath the upper line
cues.text: The bass moves from D♭ to B♭ and then A♭ while the melody stretches across longer notes. Follow those lower changes under A♭–B♭ and D♭–C♭ above: the harmony moves even when the upper line seems to linger.
cues.evidence: Bars 9–12, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly, basIb has D♭ and B♭ in bar 9, A♭ in bar 10; hautI has A♭–B♭, then D♭ falling to C♭. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: A phrase comes back
cues.text: An earlier phrase returns: A♭–B♭, then D♭ falling to C♭. Its continuation reaches F♭ before settling on E♭. Listen for the familiar contour rather than expecting every accompaniment note to be identical.
cues.evidence: Bars 17–20, occurrence 1, compared with bars 9–12, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly, hautI repeats the melodic sequence; hautII changes notes within its broken-chord figures. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Music beside the classroom
cues.text: Schubert worked as an assistant at his father’s school while composing. In 1814 he set Goethe’s Gretchen am Spinnrade; he was seventeen. His early working life combined teaching with songs and instrumental music.
cues.evidence: The Concise Oxford Dictionary of Music entry documents his school work and dates Gretchen am Spinnrade to 19 October 1814: https://www.encyclopedia.com/people/literature-and-arts/music-history-composers-and-performers-biographies/franz-schubert

cues.title: E♭ minor presses forward
cues.text: The middle section moves into E♭ minor. Accented B♭s in the melody sit over E♭–G♭–B♭ broken chords, while the bass gains its own rising triplet figures. The accompaniment continues, but melody and bass now make more pointed gestures.
cues.evidence: Bars 25–28, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. HautI accents B♭; hautII outlines E♭ minor; basIc rises E♭–F–G♭ and G♭–A♭–B♭. The score’s dynamics include forte and subsequent retreat. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The figuration moves lower
cues.text: The melody descends through E♭, D♭, C♭, A♭ and F♭, then lingers on C♭. Around it, the broken chords move into a lower register. Listen for their continued motion beneath the repeated melodic note, through the score’s very quiet writing.
cues.evidence: Bars 33–39, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. HautI descends in bar 33 and repeats C♭ in bars 35–39; basIII carries the broken chords while hautII mostly rests. DynPartCom marks ppp in bar 35. Timing aligned automatically; quiet-passage timing is provisional.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Printed in another key
cues.text: The third and fourth Impromptus of D. 899 were first published in 1857. This third piece appeared transposed into G major rather than Schubert’s G♭ major. The score used here preserves the original six-flat key.
cues.evidence: Publication date and transposition: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impromptus_(Schubert) . The original-key score is Mutopia 1193, based on Breitkopf & Härtel (1888): https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=1193

cues.title: Accents return to the melody
cues.text: C♭ falls to B♭ and A♭; the next bar continues G♭–F and E♭–D♮. The written accents pick out the descending line, while D♮ points towards E♭ as a leading note. Listen for the minor-key tension beneath the unchanged triplet motion.
cues.evidence: Bars 40–45, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly, hautI writes these descents with accents in bars 40–41 and 44–45; hautII includes D♮ in its broken chords. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: E♭ turns towards major
cues.text: G♮ replaces the minor third G♭ in the bass and broken chords, turning towards E♭ major. The melody still begins on B♭. Listen to the changed notes underneath it: a familiar melodic pitch can belong to a different mode.
cues.evidence: Bars 48–51, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. BasIe starts on G♮; hautII outlines E♭–G♮–B♭ in bar 48, and basIII continues that major triad in bar 51. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The G♭ melody returns
cues.text: The opening B♭ melody and G♭-major accompaniment return after the preceding bar’s fermata. This is a written-out return, not a repeat sign: the score continues with new bar numbers and later alters the familiar phrase.
cues.evidence: Bar 55, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. HautI restores the opening B♭ rhythm; hautII restores B♭–D♭–G♭ figuration; basIf restores the G♭–D♭ bass. Bar 54, occurrence 1, has the preceding fermata. Timing aligned automatically; no exact fermata-release time is claimed.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: Long notes across changing chords
cues.text: The returning tune rises from A♭ to B♭, then from D♭ falls to C♭. Keep following those long notes while the triplets change beneath them. The melody’s slower rhythm and the accompaniment’s continuous subdivisions remain separate layers.
cues.evidence: Bars 63–66, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly, hautI gives A♭–B♭, D♭–C♭, C♭–D♭ and F♭–E♭ in long values; hautII maintains its 6:4 groups with changing pitches. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The year of Winterreise
cues.text: The two sets of Impromptus, D. 899 and D. 935, date from 1827, also the year of Winterreise. These piano pieces and the song cycle belong to the same late period, but the Impromptus are independent works, not song transcriptions.
cues.evidence: The Impromptus’ 1827 date is documented at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impromptus_(Schubert) ; the Concise Oxford Dictionary of Music catalogue dates Winterreise, D. 911, to 1827: https://www.encyclopedia.com/people/literature-and-arts/music-history-composers-and-performers-biographies/franz-schubert

cues.title: The return is not literal
cues.text: C♭ rises through D♭ to D♮ in the melody; the next bar reaches E♭, then lowers it to E double-flat. These chromatic changes disturb the restored tune without interrupting the broken chords underneath.
cues.evidence: Bars 70–72, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly, hautI has C♭–D♭–D♮ in bar 70 and E♭–E double-flat–C♭–A♭ in bar 71; hautII retains triplet figuration. Timing aligned automatically.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The coda lowers the bass
cues.text: The melody holds close to G♭ while the bass continues downward through E double-flat and D♭, then C♭. Listen for the lowered bass notes underneath a familiar upper pitch: the coda changes the harmony rather than introducing a separate tune.
cues.evidence: Bars 75–77, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. HautI sustains G♭ in bars 75–76; basIhP has E double-flat–D♭ in bar 75 and basIi begins C♭ in bar 76. Timing aligned automatically; grace notes and trills are not individually timed claims.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: A chromatic detour before home
cues.text: The sustained upper pitch is now written F♯ rather than G♭, over D and C bass notes. It rises to G before the familiar flat-key spelling returns. Listen for the harmonic detour, not an interruption of the flowing accompaniment.
cues.evidence: Bars 79–81, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. HautI writes F♯ in bar 79 and G then C in bar 80; basIiP writes D–C in bar 79. The six-flat signature returns within bar 80. Timing aligned automatically; REPORT.md identifies this closing region as less secure.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

cues.title: The triplets finally stop
cues.text: In the closing bars, the melody thickens into chords while the broken-chord figure makes its last descent. The final bar replaces that motion with a held G♭-major chord and fermata. Follow the change from moving notes to sustained harmony.
cues.evidence: Bars 85–86, occurrence 1: Mutopia D. 899 No. 3 (1193), SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly. HautI has G♭–B♭–G♭ chords; basIII carries the final triplets in bar 85 and stops in bar 86; basIj supplies the held G♭–D♭–G♭ bass. Timing aligned automatically; the quiet close is the weakest alignment region, so no precise release is asserted.
cues.how: From the written score, timed by aligning the score to this recording (automatic; not yet checked by ear).

transitions.title: One sharpened note redirects the flowing chords
transitions.how: Bar 24 holds G♭ in the melody while the broken chord changes D♭ to D♮ near its end; below, the bass moves G♭–F. D♮ points towards E♭, reached in the bass at bar 25. The new E♭–G♭–B♭ harmony keeps G♭ and B♭ from the opening tonic chord but makes them the third and fifth of E♭ minor. The melody now accents B♭, and the bass gains rising E♭–F–G♭ and G♭–A♭–B♭ triplets. Continuous broken chords carry the join; the accents and active bass make the minor arrival different.
transitions.evidence: The B-section boundary is bar 25 at 98.189 s in score.json. Mutopia 1193, SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly: hautI sustains G♭ in 24 and accents B♭ in 25; hautII changes D♭ to D♮ in the final group of 24 and outlines E♭ minor in 25; basIc supplies G♭–F and the rising triplets. DynPartCom marks forte at 25. The span uses bars 23–27. The analysis shows increased relative level and brightness around 1:40 and E♭-minor pitch content. Harmonic claims come from the written notes; timing remains provisional.

transitions.title: A held dominant releases the opening melody
transitions.how: After E♭ major in bar 51, A♭ minor’s C♭ reappears in bars 52–53. The bass moves through A♭ and a trilled G♭ to F in 54, beneath D♭–F–A♭–C♭: D♭7 in first inversion. E double-flat briefly adds a flattened ninth. A fermata suspends the figuration while the melody holds C♭. At 55, C♭ falls to B♭ and the bass rises F–G♭; the opening G♭-major melody and broken chords return pianissimo. The triplet texture survives the tonal detour, but the held dominant makes the release audible.
transitions.evidence: The A′ boundary is bar 55 at 218.961 s. Mutopia 1193, SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly: basIII/hautII give E♭ major and A♭ minor in 51–53; basIeP gives the bar-53 G♭ trill; basII holds F in 54 while hautII and basIf supply the dominant-seventh and E-double-flat notes and fermatas. HautI resolves C♭–B♭ at 54–55; DynPartCom reaches pp before the return. The analysis has boundaries at 3:24 and 3:28 and a quiet 3:35 window; the form relation supports the written-out return. The span is bars 51–56. REPORT.md flags this transition’s timing as needing aural review.

transitions.title: The melody stays while the bass descends
transitions.how: The phrase reaches G♭ major in bar 74, but the bass does not stay there. Its G♭–F♭ continues through E double-flat and D♭ in 75 to C♭ in 76, while the melody remains centred on G♭. Over E double-flat, the accompaniment spells C♭–E double-flat–G♭: C♭ minor in first inversion, borrowing the minor subdominant rather than settling on the tonic. The D♭ bass then supports G♭–B♭–F♭ before C♭ minor returns. The continuing triplets and sustained upper G♭ join the coda to the familiar phrase while the lower line changes its harmony.
transitions.evidence: The Coda boundary is bar 75 at 300.475 s, near the analysis’s 4:58 novelty boundary. Mutopia 1193, SchubertF-D899-3-Impromptu.ly: basIhP/basIi write the bass descent in 74–76; hautII has G♭–C♭–E double-flat, then G♭–B♭–F♭ in 75, returning to the former chord at the start of 76; hautI sustains and decorates G♭. score.json supplies the bar-73-to-78 span. The analysis’s 5:00 window changes bass pitch content, but the chord names are editorial score readings. Timing, especially ornaments and the later quiet close, remains provisional.

facts: Vienna Stadtkonvikt, 1808–13; composition with Antonio Salieri, 1812–16
Assistant in his father’s school; music tutor to the Esterházy family at Zseliz in 1818 and 1824; thereafter chiefly an independent composer
Johann Michael Vogl · Josef von Spaun · Franz von Schober · Johann Mayrhofer · Moritz von Schwind
More than 600 songs; symphonies, chamber music, piano sonatas and duets, masses and music for the stage
composer.background:
Schubert grew up in a schoolmaster’s household in Himmelpfortgrund, then a suburb of Vienna. His father taught him violin, his brother Ignaz taught him piano, and the parish musician Michael Holzer supplied further instruction. Family quartet sessions put Franz on viola, between the melody and the bass: he knew chamber music from an inner part. In 1808 he entered the imperial chapel choir and the Stadtkonvikt boarding school. Its orchestra introduced him to Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven as a player, while Antonio Salieri began giving him composition lessons in 1812.

After leaving the school in 1813, he trained as a teacher and became an assistant in his father’s classroom. Composition continued around the timetable. Gretchen am Spinnrade, dated 19 October 1814, gives Goethe’s girl a right-hand spinning wheel, a left-hand treadle and a vocal line that repeatedly tries to escape them. Schubert was seventeen. In 1815 he wrote roughly 140 songs, including Erlkönig, as well as symphonies, church music and stage works. Voice and piano already carried distinct dramatic responsibilities in his songs.
composer.epithet: A Viennese songwriter who made the piano an equal narrator, and carried the harmonic dislocations of the Lied into symphonies and chamber music.
